audience: Primary care clinicians in NHS Dumfries and Galloway
in_scope: Recognition and initial assessment of suspected myeloma
Interpretation of common abnormal blood/urine findings suggestive of plasma cell dyscrasia
Primary care baseline investigations before referral where safe
Immediate admission red flags and urgency tiers for referral
MGUS diagnosis follow-up framework in primary care and re-referral triggers
out_of_scope: Detailed inpatient management of hypercalcaemia, sepsis, spinal cord compression
core_questions: When should same-day admission be arranged?
Which patients need USOC vs urgent non-cancer outpatient referral?
How should MGUS be monitored in primary care and when should follow-up interval change?
summary: Single combined pathway for myeloma suspicion and established MGUS follow-up.
Prioritises red flags, referral urgency, and practical GP investigation sequence.
Uses D&G urgency labels and explicit re-referral triggers.
